claim: The labelled note on the result row shows only the characters typed instead of the whole value that matched. Measured: "786" → 6 rows, 4 labelled notes, 4 showing only what was typed

instrument.positive_control: Two, in the same run and on the same row type. (1) C146216 PASSES: typing part of a contact's email returns a note carrying the WHOLE address, so the reader reports 'full value' when a full value is drawn. (2) On the Customers tab, typing 3286 returns six rows all showing whole telephone numbers such as '(264) 328-6723'. A reader that finds those and still reports 'only what was typed' elsewhere is working.
instrument.independent_repeat: Varied the input rather than replaying it: every case is searched twice, once with the term the case supplies and once with a different, shorter fragment of the same value. The fault also reproduced across two DIFFERENT BUILDS - v26.39.1-97cad2c and v26.39.2-51a35e1, staging having been redeployed mid-session.
instrument.state_recorded: Admin on app.staging.shopview.com, build v26.39.2-51a35e1, 29 September 2026, viewport 1440x900. Pointer moved to 0,0 and read back with document.elementFromPoint before each read and again after the tab switch. Each query typed fresh into an emptied box; the record type's own tab opened deliberately, because the All tab lists only five rows per group.
instrument.what_would_make_this_my_fault: Three ways, all ruled out and two of which I actually hit. (1) TYPING THE WHOLE VALUE. A note identical to the query is correct output when the query IS the value, and is indistinguishable from the fault - my first classifier counted those as failures. No verdict here rests on a whole-value query; where the case supplies one, a proper fragment was searched instead. (2) AN UNREACHED STATE. Where the fragment matches nothing, no labelled note comes back, which says nothing about the product; those cases are recorded as not judged, not failed. (3) READING THE WRONG ELEMENT. The note is located by its shape ('Label: value') across every meta part on the row, not by a class name chosen in advance - a selector picked from one row type and reused produced a false finding earlier today on the customer badge.

note: Same cause as the Q3 ticket prepared in build/global-search/q3-evidence-2026-09-29. Not a new ticket per case.
